description: AWH-Geo is X's geospatial model for assessing drinking-water production from atmospheric water harvesters. It contains Google Colab notebooks using Earth Engine to combine device-output curves with weather and population layers. Outputs include daily production potential, shortfall statistics and populations within specified production thresholds. The documented global analysis uses hourly ERA5-Land weather at nine-kilometre resolution for 2010-2019 and a one-kilometre population layer based on 2017 WorldPop data. Python source is available through GitHub free under Apache-2.0; upstream data and Google services retain separate terms. A limitation is that full threshold experiments may exceed Earth Engine storage quotas, and execution requires the user's own Google service accounts. The model supports decentralised drinking-water supply and device-design simulations. WorldPop-derived data are an input, and QGIS (platform-qgis) provides related spatial analysis. The README's in-review paper note is outdated: the describing Nature article was published in 2021.
